message.content:
Nasal atomizer assemblies (e.g., MAD Nasal) have been classified in CBP rulings. The likely candidates are heading 9018 (medical instruments) or 9617/9616 (atomizers). Heading 9616 covers scent sprays and similar toilet sprays, which doesn't fit medical use. Heading 9018.90 covers other instruments and appliances for medical use. Parts and accessories of syringes fall under 9018.31 (syringes, with or without needles), with parts under 9018.31.00 as well. Since this is an atomizer that attaches to a syringe, it is likely classified as 9018.90.80 (other instruments and appliances) or as a part of an item in 9018.

For the MAD Nasal device, I recall ruling NY N-series classifying it in 9018.90.8000. Others classify mucosal atomization devices as "other instruments and appliances" under 9018.90.75 (other: electro-medical) or 9018.90.80. I will go with 9018.90.8000.

For unassembled components imported together, GRI 2(a) treats them as the assembled article.

{"hts_code": "9018.90.8000", "reason": "The unassembled atomizer tip and body are classified under GRI 2(a) as the finished nasal atomization device, which is an other medical instrument or appliance of heading 9018."}
